chunks: And they said, 'What is [the matter] with this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? But why was there not sent down to him an angel that he would be with him a warner?'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Quraysh question Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) human habits like eating and walking in markets?
ai.summary: In Surah Al-Furqan, the Quraysh criticized Prophet Muhammad’s (SAWW) mundane human habits, such as eating and walking in markets, demanding an angelic companion to validate his prophethood. Shia scholars emphasize that this verse establishes the principle of *insaniyyat al-nabi* (the humanity of the Prophet), demonstrating that divine messengers share human experiences to serve as relatable models (*uswa hasana*) for their communities. This counters the notion that spiritual authority requires supernatural detachment, affirming that prophethood is a human condition elevated by divine selection.
